metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Taiwan ROC strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Hey Omar, have you thought about getting Adam a bottle of champagne for the celebration? I mean, it’s a big deal, right? It could be a cool gift.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I... I don't think champagne is a good idea. It's not really suitable for everyone, and we should consider something more meaningful. Maybe something personal that Adam would appreciate? What do you think about a nice pen or a book?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Hmm, I get that. But a bottle of champagne feels like a classic celebratory gift. I mean, it’s not just about the drink itself—it’s about marking the occasion. Plus, don’t you think it’s... I don’t know, a little fun? What do you think about that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I understand it's a classic gift, but... I feel like it doesn't really represent what Adam has achieved. Celebrating is important, but I want to give something that shows how proud we are of him. A personal gift will mean more, I think. What if we talk about something else?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I see your point, but it's not just about pride, right? Sometimes it's about having fun and enjoying the moment. Speaking of pride, I’ve been thinking about this a lot lately. Do you strongly agree that one of your main goals in life has been to make your parents proud?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our culture, making parents proud is *everything*. It’s not just a goal; it’s a duty. You don’t understand the weight of that. You can’t just enjoy the moment without considering family honor. It shapes who we are. Fun is... secondary. In our way, we celebrate achievements by showing respect to our families. That’s how it works.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: Yeah, I get that it’s important, but honestly, I don’t really think it’s my main goal. I feel like there’s so much more to life than just trying to please my parents. I mean, wouldn’t you agree that finding your own path is just as valuable?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I can see that you feel differently, but for me, making my parents proud is *the* priority. Finding your own path is important too, but it can’t overshadow our responsibilities. In my culture, honoring family is a core value. I just... I can't separate that from my goals in life.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I understand that’s how you feel, but I still think it’s okay to have your own aspirations too. I mean, shouldn’t we all define success for ourselves instead of just following what’s expected? It just seems like there’s more to life than fitting into that mold. Don’t you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I get what you're saying, but... I just can't agree. For me, success *is* tied to my family's pride. It's a part of who I am. We all have different views, and that's okay, but I really believe that honoring my parents is what gives my life meaning. I don't want to lose that.
turns.label: Defense

positive.mediator_utterance: I'm hearing that both of you deeply care about honoring Adam's achievement and showing genuine respect. Could we explore what 'respect' looks like from each of your perspectives? What matters most to you about how we recognize someone's hard work and success?
